- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or lags; adjust upward to reflect sentiment-driven momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 1–3%.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; re-estimate mean reversion toward prior 7–14 day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment swings; dampen volatility in later days (e.g., days 15–30) by 10–20% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “+0.33” or “-0.33” oscillations, model often misreads trend; use sentiment-weighted moving average (e.g., 5-day sentiment filter) to smooth forecast.
